summary:
First audit these two packages have ever had. CAPACITY has SEVEN entry points (new_valve, observe, caps, startup_refusals, state, restore, counters) of which SIX are NotImplementedError stubs -- new_valve is the only body. EVAL has NINE (curve_period, curve_probe, holdout_probe, null_excess, generate, coherence, verdicts, wrongness_probe, verification_fit) of which EIGHT are stubs -- curve_period is the only body. Counted by `grep -c NotImplementedError src/capacity/api.py src/eval/api.py` -> 6 and 8, against the seven and nine `def` at module level, and matching the surfaces docs/04_CONTRACT.md:502 and :538 declare.

THE DEFAULTS, since the owner asked and nobody had read these files. CAP ships the valve OFF: CAP_TARGETS='off' (choices off|experts|vocab|both), CAP_FAB_START=0, CAP_VOCAB_START=0 (both SENTINELS meaning 'start at the hard ceiling, no room to earn'), CAP_LIFT=0.08, CAP_LIFT_MIN=8, CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=20000 (unit Windows), CAP_STALL_BAND=0.002. So on a stock run NOTHING in this package can fire, and its four wires resolve to d_expert_slots=4096, d_vocab_slots=4096, d_mask_dead_rows=False, d_operating_population=1844.
THE DEFAULT THAT WILL SURPRISE: turning CAP_TARGETS on is NOT enough to arm the expert valve. The fab_start sentinel resolves to the HARD ceiling 4096, while the cull's settling point (d_operating_population = FAB.pressure x FAB.slots = 0.45 x 4096) is 1844. A soft cap above the settling point is a cap the population never reaches, so it never pins, the pin clock never accumulates, and the valve is dead while every report line says it is armed -- capacity's own words. CAP.startup_refusals is the declared place that refuses this and it is a stub, so today nothing catches it. Verified by building CAP and printing the four wires.
EVAL ships all seventeen levers ON in the sense that both flags are True: EVAL_GENERATE=True, EVAL_WRONGNESS=True. Sizes: EVAL_WINDOWS=64, EVAL_HOLDOUT_WINDOWS=32, EVAL_NULL_DRAWS=5, EVAL_COH_SEEDS=16, EVAL_COH_LEN=384, EVAL_GEN_SAMPLES=4, EVAL_GEN_DOMAINS=4, EVAL_GEN_LEN=200, EVAL_GEN_TEMP=0.7, EVAL_CURVE_EVERY=2000 (Windows), EVAL_GENUINE_MIN=20, EVAL_GENUINE_SIL=0.10, EVAL_AFF_MIN=0.10, EVAL_WRONG_INJECT=8, EVAL_VERIFY_FIT_STEPS=3000 (Steps). EVAL declares NO wires and receives none -- confirmed against spine/assemble.py's COUPLINGS, where no row names EVAL as src or dst.
THE EVAL DEFAULT THAT WILL SURPRISE: EVAL_CURVE_EVERY=2000 Windows against a shipped run of 506-937 windows (DATA_STREAM_BYTES=120000, LM_CTX=128, RUN_EPOCHS=1, all verified live) means the learning-curve probe NEVER FIRES at the defaults -- so CKPT's best-checkpoint retention can never receive a value either. That is ISSUES P1-C11 and it is already recorded in the tree; I am confirming it holds, not discovering it.

CONTRACT AUDIT RESULT. Both live bodies read EXACTLY the levers and wires their LEVERS READ / WIRES READ lines name -- no more, no less (checked by parsing every docstring block against each LeverSet's _levers: zero levers named-but-not-declared, zero declared-but-unnamed across all 7 CAP and 17 EVAL levers, and all four CAP wires named). NO CAP OR EVAL LEVER IS WITHOUT A READER. Neither package mints an RNG stream, so no fifth rng_for collision was created; 'eval' is already declared as a drawn parent in spine/compose.py::RNG_SUBSYSTEMS with its 'eval.holdout.<domain>' children derived by the package, which is the established pattern and not a re-issue. Units are right in both bodies: EVAL.curve_period returns units.Windows and Steps appears in EVAL only on verify_fit_steps, which is a genuine optimizer-step length in a loop with no windows in it.

SEVEN DEFECTS FOUND, SIX FIXED. One HIGH (the filed Gate defect, reproduced and fixed and now proven honest on all EIGHT corners rather than the four asked for -- the filed report and its suggested fix both missed that CAP_TARGETS=experts is broken too, in the opposite direction). Two MEDIUM code defects nobody had filed (an explicitly-typed CAP_FAB_START=0 losing the sentinel and resolving a soft cap of ZERO; four dataclass Clock defaults shared as ONE object across every Valve in the process). Two MEDIUM stale-prose defects, each asserting an absence the tree has already filled. Two LOW. The suite is green: ownership 12+18, contract 14+46, census 7, assemble 9, couplings 4, derive 575 oracle cases -- 0 failing anywhere. ONE THING LEFT UNFINISHED and it is a signature question I am not allowed to settle alone; it is written into the tree rather than patched or dropped.

recommendation.chose: For the HIGH finding: key cap.vocab_arm_honest's REACHABILITY on whether the VOCABULARY ARM is armed -- `targets in ('vocab','both')` -- rather than on `targets == 'off'` as the filed fix proposed, and print `targets` against 'vocab|both' as the unreachable arm's arithmetic, mirroring the sibling cap.valve, with LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS's value carried in the reason so nothing is hidden. Implemented as a three-way if/elif/else lifted out of the tuple, in src/capacity/api.py::new_valve.
recommendation.alternatives: (A) The fix as filed in .rework/audits/r2_sweep_full.json: route `targets == "off"` to the unreachable branch. COST: it repairs 1 of the 2 broken corners and leaves the other. (B) What I did: reachability keyed on the arm. COST: one extra branch and one extra reason string. (C) Emit no vocab gate at all when the arm is off. COST: the report then has one gate on some runs and two on others, so a reader must distinguish ABSENT from UNREACHABLE -- and spine/compose.py's own comment says 'a subsystem ABSENT never asked... those are two different statements'. It replaces a collapsed distinction with a different collapsed distinction. (D) Split the valve into cap.expert_arm / cap.vocab_arm gates. COST: renames a declared gate name and changes the DID IT FIRE contract for a report surface other packages print beside; out of proportion to a wrong predicate.
recommendation.evidence: The eight-corner run separates (A) from (B) outright, and it is the reason I did not take the filed fix. BEFORE, at CAP_TARGETS=experts (an arm longrun.sh:470 names as the one clean read of the expert valve, so not a hypothetical configuration): with LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1 the gate printed 'Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: FIRED (True vs True)' -- certifying as HONEST a vocabulary lift that run will never attempt -- and with LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0 it printed 'UNREACHABLE (False vs True) -- LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: the vocabulary arm can lift...', a reason that is FALSE on that configuration. Fix (A) touches neither corner, because neither goes through `targets == "off"`. AFTER, both read 'Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: UNREACHABLE (experts vs vocab|both) -- CAP_TARGETS=experts: the valve's vocabulary arm is not armed...'. The two corners the sweep filed are fixed as well: shipped default (off, 0) goes from 'armed, did not fire (False vs True)' to 'UNREACHABLE (off vs vocab|both)'. The two corners that were already right (vocab/both x mask 0/1) are unchanged, which is the control.
recommendation.measurement: The measurement that settles it, and the one I ran: build CAP at all EIGHT combinations of CAP_TARGETS in (off, experts, vocab, both) x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS in (0, 1) and assert that cap.vocab_arm_honest.reachable is True on exactly the four where a vocabulary lift is possible, i.e. targets in (vocab, both). Before: reachable on 5 of 8 (off/0, off/1, experts/1, vocab/1, both/1), wrong on 4 of those 8 (off x {0,1} and experts x {0,1}). After: reachable on exactly 4 of 8, and they are the right four. BOTH NUMBERS CORRECTED 2026-09-04 BY THE REPAIR PASS, and the correction is the point rather than the arithmetic: this field read 6 of 8 before and 4 of 8 after. Measured, the pre-fix predicate (mask_dead or targets == off) is reachable on FIVE, not six; and the fix AS SHIPPED left it reachable on TWO, not four, because the mask arm declared UNREACHABLE at vocab/0 and both/0 as well -- which this report's own proof field states correctly. So the assertion as written FAILED on the tree this report produced, and a reader re-running it would have filed a correct gate as broken. It PASSES now: the repair pass ruled the mask-off arm an UNMET CONDITION rather than an unreachable one (capacity/api.py::new_valve, the third branch of the vocabulary gate), so reachable is True on exactly vocab x {0,1} and both x {0,1}. Established by rebuilding all eight corners three times: against git 8cb00e3 (5 of 8), against this report's own HEAD (2 of 8), and against the repaired tree (4 of 8). Script kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/repro_gates8.py. Note the four-corner grid the task asked for could not have separated (A) from (B) -- it is precisely the two `experts` corners that do, which is why I widened it.

changed.title: HIGH (filed, reproduced, fixed): Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest collapsed UNREACHABLE into armed-but-0 on the shipped defaults -- and, unrecorded by the filing, printed FIRED for an arm that cannot fire at CAP_TARGETS=experts
changed.what_changed: src/capacity/api.py::new_valve. The gate was `Gate("cap.vocab_arm_honest", mask_dead, mask_dead, True) if mask_dead or targets == "off" else Gate(..., reachable=False, ...)`. Because spine/gate.py::Gate defaults reachable=True, `mask_dead=False and targets=='off'` fell into the REACHABLE branch and printed a measurement for a mechanism that cannot run; and because the predicate never mentioned the arm, `targets=='experts'` printed FIRED (mask on) or a false reason (mask off). Replaced by a three-way branch on `targets not in ("vocab","both")` / `mask_dead` / else, hoisted out of the tuple so all three states are readable side by side, with the unreachable arm printing `targets` vs 'vocab|both' the way the sibling cap.valve prints `targets` vs 'off'.
changed.proof: BEFORE, `python3` building CAP through spine.assemble at the shipped defaults printed `Gate cap.valve: UNREACHABLE (off vs off) -- CAP_TARGETS=off: ...` beside `Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: armed, did not fire (False vs True)` -- two gates evaluating the same condition and reaching opposite reachability verdicts. Widening to all eight corners showed two MORE wrong readings the filing did not have: `CAP_TARGETS=experts LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1` -> `Gate cap.vocab_arm_honest: FIRED (True vs True)`, and `CAP_TARGETS=experts LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0` -> `UNREACHABLE (False vs True) -- LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: the vocabulary arm can lift, ...` (false: it cannot). AFTER, the same eight corners read: off x{0,1} -> `UNREACHABLE (off vs vocab|both)`; experts x{0,1} -> `UNREACHABLE (experts vs vocab|both)`; vocab/both x mask=0 -> `UNREACHABLE (False vs True) -- LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0: ...`; vocab/both x mask=1 -> `FIRED (True vs True)`. cap.valve is unchanged on all eight.

changed.title: MEDIUM (new): an explicitly-set CAP_FAB_START=0 lost the sentinel and resolved a soft expert cap of ZERO -- one number meaning two things depending on whether the environment supplied it
changed.what_changed: src/capacity/api.py::new_valve, the `_resolve` helper. `if given: return int(asked), ...` returned the raw value, so 0 meant 'the hard ceiling' when it came from the declared default and 'a soft cap of literally zero' when the operator typed the documented sentinel. Now the sentinel is tested on the VALUE: an explicit 0 returns the hard ceiling with origin `operator (fab_start=0, the sentinel) -> hard ceiling 4096`, so provenance is still recorded and the documented precedence (explicit request beats checkpoint beats default sentinel) is unchanged.
changed.proof: BEFORE: building with {'CAP_TARGETS':'both','CAP_FAB_START':'0','CAP_VOCAB_START':'0'} printed `cap_experts=0 cap_vocab=0` with origin `('operator (fab_start=0)', 'operator (vocab_start=0)')`, against a hard ceiling of 4096 -- while leaving the same lever UNSET printed `cap_experts=4096 cap_vocab=4096`. A soft cap of 0 is C30 by construction: capacity/levers.py's own fab_start comment records `min(_nb, _cap_fab[0] - fab.n())` going negative and freezing growth for the whole run with nothing in the log. AFTER: the same build prints `cap_experts=4096 cap_vocab=4096` with origin `('operator (fab_start=0, the sentinel) -> hard ceiling 4096', 'operator (vocab_start=0, the sentinel) -> hard ceiling 4096')`, and the control `CAP_FAB_START=256` still gives `cap_experts=256`, origin `operator (fab_start=256)`.

changed.title: MEDIUM (new): the Valve dataclass's four Clock defaults were ONE shared object per field across every Valve in the process -- a mutable default that dataclasses' own guard cannot see
changed.what_changed: src/capacity/api.py, the Valve record. `pin_experts: object = U.Windows(0)` (and pin_vocab, hi_pin_experts, hi_pin_vocab) evaluated the constructor once at class creation. dataclasses only refuses UNHASHABLE defaults and spine/units.py's Clock defines __hash__, so it sailed through. All four are now `dataclasses.field(default_factory=lambda: U.Windows(0))`, with the reasoning recorded on the record.
changed.proof: BEFORE: `a=Valve(1,2); b=Valve(3,4)` gave `a.pin_experts is b.pin_experts -> True` and `a.hi_pin_vocab is b.hi_pin_vocab -> True`; then `a.pin_experts.n = 999` made `b.pin_experts` read `999 windows` AND made a brand-new `Valve(5,6).pin_experts` read `999 windows`. Clock has `__slots__=('n',)` and no __setattr__ guard, so `valve.pin_experts.n += dstep` -- the natural in-place spelling for accumulating a clock, which CAP.observe is stubbed to do -- is the mutation that triggers it, and the result is an unearned pin clock on every later Valve, which is the M38 family. AFTER: the same script prints `shared: False False` and `b.pin_experts = 0 windows | fresh Valve = 0 windows`.

changed.title: MEDIUM (new): capacity/levers.py's WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT section asserted that NONE of CAP's wires exists, and named a source prefix that no longer exists -- a false absence that would push a port agent over the wire budget
changed.what_changed: src/capacity/levers.py::<module>. The section read 'NONE OF THE FOUR IS IN spine/assemble.py's COUPLINGS TODAY... there are no CAP wires to be found unread, because there are no CAP wires', said the only d_expert_slots row targeted DOM, said no d_vocab_slots row existed at all, said FAB.d_cap_lift_period and TOK.d_cap_lift_period source from a prefix named TRAIN, and quoted O4 as '10 declared destinations, 0 declared-but-unread, 10 deferred'. Rewritten to the tree as it is, with each wire's reader named as `capacity/api.py::<symbol>`, d_operating_population added (the section omitted it entirely), and the stale claims quoted so the correction is auditable rather than silent.
changed.proof: `grep -n 'dst="' src/spine/assemble.py` lists `dst="CAP.d_expert_slots"`, `dst="CAP.d_vocab_slots"`, `dst="CAP.d_mask_dead_rows"` and `dst="CAP.d_operating_population"`. Both cap-lift rows read `src=("OPT.batch_windows", "CAP.pin_windows")`, not TRAIN -- and spine/assemble.py::_check_endpoints's own docstring records TRAIN.grow_cap_every as corrected to CAP.pin_windows. `python3 tests/test_ownership.py` prints `PASS O4 ... 23 declared destination(s), 20 distinct d_ field(s) read at 28 site(s); 0 declared-but-unread, 0 deferred`, not 10/10. THE COST OF LEAVING IT: the section tells whoever ports the valve to ADD four couplings, and spine/wire.py::WIRE_BUDGET is 25 against 23 already recorded, so acting on it fails at build() with an over-budget refusal, on work already done.

changed.title: MEDIUM (new): eval/levers.py asserted the Windows-vs-Steps conflict with the spine as OPEN after the spine settled it, and told a reader the conversion it needs does not exist
changed.what_changed: src/eval/levers.py::<module>, DEFECT 2. It read 'THE CONFLICT WITH THE SPINE, STATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED', claimed 'derive.flush_period REFUSES anything but Steps... so there is today NO legal conversion from a Windows-typed cadence to the flush clock', and demanded that 'either spine.derive gains a Windows->Flushes conversion or FAB.manage_every and TRAIN.grow_cap_every change kind'. All three clauses are false against the current tree, and its own sibling capacity/levers.py::<module> already records the settlement -- so two files I own contradicted each other about the project's flagship unit defect. Rewritten to state what is now true, keeping the quoted old claims.
changed.proof: `spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows` exists and is exactly the Windows->Flushes conversion, declared beside flush_period on purpose so flush_period keeps refusing a Windows. spine/assemble.py's FAB.d_manage_period and FAB.d_cap_lift_period rows both call `derive.flush_period_windows(Windows(...), r['OPT'].batch_windows)`, and the FAB row's own `why` says 'the Steps assumption is withdrawn and the conversion is derive.flush_period_windows'. There is no package TRAIN and no lever grow_cap_every: `grep -n 'grow_cap_every' src/spine/assemble.py` returns only prose recording the correction. NOT FIXED BY ME AND NOT MINE: the identical stale paragraph survives in src/memory/levers.py:55-60, which is outside src/capacity and src/eval.

changed.title: LOW (new): capacity/levers.py's irreducible-coupling comment carried an operating-population figure twice the number the wire delivers
changed.what_changed: src/capacity/levers.py, the fab_start declaration comment. It read 'the cull settling point FAB_PRESSURE x FAB_SLOTS (0.45 x 8192 = 3686 at the launch config)'. FAB.slots defaults to 4096 and no configuration in this tree sets 8192. Corrected to the number the wire actually delivers, with the reader (capacity/api.py::startup_refusals) and the wire (d_operating_population) named.
changed.proof: `cfgs['CAP'].d_operating_population` -> 1844 and `cfgs['FAB'].slots` -> 4096, `cfgs['FAB'].pressure` -> 0.45, all read off a live build. `grep -rn 'FAB_SLOTS\|FAB_NMAX' --include=*.sh --include=*.py .` finds 8192 only inside ramp_test.py's illustration; self_organize.py:196 declares FAB_NMAX's default as 4096. THE DIRECTION MATTERS: 3686 is twice 1844 the wrong way, so a soft cap of 3000 -- which every sched_* arm used -- passes a check against 3686 and sits ABOVE 1844, which is exactly the 'valve dead while looking armed' failure the sentence exists to prevent.

changed.title: LOW (new): three DID IT FIRE names in capacity/api.py had no declared home, the Valve RECORD TYPES line omitted two of its own fields, and eval/api.py miscounted the sibling period accessors
changed.what_changed: src/capacity/api.py: CAP.state declared `DID IT FIRE: valve.state_written` and CAP.restore declared `valve.state_restored, valve.state_refused` -- none is a field of Valve and none is produced anywhere, so the signals saying the checkpoint carried the valve's earned state had no home a reader could find. Re-pointed at the declared ledger, `valve.counters["cap.state_written"]` etc. The module's RECORD TYPES line said '(P4 defines them)' of Valve, which is declared in that very file, and its Valve row omitted `counters` and `gates` -- the two fields where new_valve actually parks the hard ceilings and the Gate readings; both corrected. src/eval/api.py::curve_period said 'NOT A STUB, AND THE THREE SIBLINGS ARE NOT EITHER' where there are FOUR (DOM.manage_period, FAB.manage_period, MEM.rekey_period, CKPT.save_period).
changed.proof: `grep -n 'state_written\|state_restored\|state_refused' src/capacity/api.py` found them only inside the two DID IT FIRE lines, and `Valve.__dataclass_fields__` contains no such name. docs/04_CONTRACT.md:2044 reads 'The **five** accessors -- EVAL.curve_period, DOM.manage_period, FAB.manage_period, MEM.rekey_period, CKPT.save_period' and adds '(This sentence said "four" until 2026-09-03... four is a word, and the check reads digits)' -- so eval/api.py carried the identical word-number off-by-one, one row over, and K13 cannot see either. All four siblings verified stub-free. The same paragraph's other count, 'all 35 levers that declare a Clock unit', I checked and it is EXACTLY right: 35 across the thirteen packages.

unfinished.title: EVAL.verification_fit declares a Gate whose input the frozen signature has no channel for, and EVAL.curve_probe must return a CurveReading field it cannot obtain
unfinished.reason: Both need a SIGNATURE change, and signatures are declared in docs/04_CONTRACT.md, which is outside my ownership; tests/test_contract.py's K1 compares the document and the tree in both directions, so widening a signature here alone is a failing suite and a second source of truth. The alternative -- a wire -- would spend one of the two edges spine/wire.py::WIRE_BUDGET has left in the whole tree, and the standing instruction is to report a wire rather than spend it. Deleting the Gate or the field to make the file self-consistent is the compromise I am forbidden to make.
unfinished.detail: VERIFIED PARTIAL PROGRESS: the gap is proven and is now WRITTEN INTO src/eval/api.py's module docstring and into verification_fit's DID IT FIRE line, with both candidate repairs and their costs, so it is a recorded gap rather than a silent one. (1) verification_fit's signature is `(ev: Config, *, store_copy, rng)` and its DID IT FIRE declares 'the Gate on `verify != "off"` -- ... rendered from the value the composition root passed'. There is no such parameter; MEM's `verify` is MEM's lever; EVAL declares no wires and receives none; and src/memory/api.py's Store carries no verify field (its __slots__ are the entry arrays, the block partition and the census, checked), so it cannot be recovered from store_copy either. spine/compose.py's deferral for this entry point names only the missing store_copy, not this. (2) curve_probe's signature is `(ev, *, units_by_domain, logits_fn, rng)` and the CurveReading it returns is documented as carrying `step` -- RUN's window counter, which no argument supplies and which EVAL owns no clock for. RECOMMENDED REPAIR, cheaper of the two: a keyword argument (`step=`, and `verify_mode=` or the value carried on MEM's Store), which costs one edit in docs/04_CONTRACT.md and one in the composition root's row when P5/P6 land these rows. A wire buys nothing the argument does not here, because the value is consumed by an instrument and never by a mechanism -- so it is the wrong thing to spend budget on.
